items.text: Code convention (user rule, stated 2026-11-04): never use positional boolean parameters; use an options object instead, since `parse(x, true)` tells nothing at the call site. This is why the API is `parse(str, { requireUnit: true })`, and the agent agreed to follow the rule for anything else added.

items.text: As of 2026-11-04, `parse` in ms has an opt-in `requireUnit` option via a `ParseOptions` interface in `src/index.ts`: `parse(str, { requireUnit: true })` returns NaN for unitless strings like "30", "1.5", "-5". Default behaviour is unchanged (`parse('30')` is still 30, also with `requireUnit: false`). `ms()` and `parseStrict` do not take the option. Motivation: bare numbers like "30" in config files get read as 30 milliseconds, which is almost always a mistake. Tests are in `src/parse.test.ts` and the README has a "Requiring a unit" section; the change was uncommitted when reported.

items.text: The ms project began on 2012-03-07 with an 'Initial import as repository.' by Guillermo Rauch, followed by a fix for latest mocha. On 2012-03-08 tubalmartin contributed a performance rewrite ('Smaller footprint 2.8x better performance. Passes all unit tests.').

In July–August 2025 the ms project ran a modernization toward a new major version (next major targets 4.x) with breaking changes: `ms` moved to a named export (#243), IE support dropped (#244), minimum Node set to 18 with CI on 20/22/24 (#226), then ESM-only and Node 18 dropped (#264), and the default export removed (#267). The default export had briefly been added back (#259) before being removed again. Node 16 was too old to upgrade tooling such as pnpm, jest and husky.
